title: Get started with lazer
text: Reading set files normally takes small pipeline: list.files(), loop purrr::map(), manual naming. read_files() one call: expands paths glue syntax, checks every file exists reading anything, picks reader extension, names results. single path returns object directly; several return named list. Supported formats: csv, tsv, parquet, feather, xlsx, xls, rds, sas7bdat, sav, por, xpt, dta, json, ndjson, jsonl, yaml, yml, txt. CSV files read semicolon-separated decimal comma, Danish convention; pass reader = readr::read_csv comma-separated files. reader works: file fails read stop others; failures reported together end, file. Column names lowercased default (.lowercase = FALSE keep ). Binding. = "bind" stacks files, .id records row came (numeric names ). column’s types combined across files, warning names , column re-typed readr::parse_guess(); every column keeps type. daos::view_types() shows file differs. Unpacking. = "unpack" assigns file variable calling environment, refuses overwrite existing ones unless .overwrite = TRUE.
code: df  <- read_files("data/results.parquet") lst <- read_files("data/dat{0:9}.parquet", names = 0:9) read_files("data/dat{0:9}.parquet",            reader = \(x) arrow::read_parquet(x, col_select = 1:5)) read_files("data/dat{2020:2024}.parquet", names = 2020:2024,            out = "bind", .id = "year") read_files("data/dat{0:9}.parquet", names = paste0("dat", 0:9), out = "unpack")
